answer.rationale: P99 latency spike to 5x target coincides temporally with release 2 hours ago during heavy settlement write load. Memory_b1 demonstrates rollback cleared a checkout error spike without customer impact; memory_b6 shows staged release gating catches regressions. The release is the only new variable in a system that normally handles peak settlement traffic (memory_b3 shows successful capacity absorption). Rollback is fastest path to restore baseline latency while preserving all writes—critical during peak settlement. Other options (capacity, failover, circuit breaker) assume the underlying system is sound; routing reads does not address write-path latency. With one intervention window, rollback tests the hypothesis that the release introduced the regression; if latency recovers, causation is confirmed. If it does not, the write path itself is degraded and next window can pursue capacity or failover with clearer signal.
